content_of_post_to_comment:
I want to take control of my life again. I’m 27 years old. I’m an English teacher, and it’s been four years since I graduated. I had dreams and goals, but because of my own lack of discipline, I couldn’t pass the exam to become a public-school teacher. If I can find a job, I’m planning to work at a language school.

In Turkey, if I become a public-school teacher, I would earn around $1,550 a month, whereas at a language school or private school, I would earn around $620.

After graduating four years ago, I spent two and a half years at home preparing for the public-school teaching exam. During that time, I also gave online English lessons, but I never managed to fully focus on the exam. I don’t know whether I was simply lazy or whether my brain was somehow avoiding studying, but I couldn’t make it work.

I also tried to quit porn and practice Nopor., but I wasn’t successful. Maybe pornography has played a role in why my life has turned out this way; I honestly don’t know.

Two months ago, I was hospitalized because of a pneumothorax. My Taiwanese girlfriend even came to visit me in the hospital. She wants me to pass the exam in Turkey, become a teacher, and build a stable life for myself here. But she also supports me by saying that if things don’t work out for me in Turkey, I can come to Taiwan and live with her.

I really want to take control of my life again. I want to start accomplishing things. Ever since I graduated, I feel like I’ve been stuck in the same place. I feel like a failure because I haven’t made the progress I wanted to make.

My father has cancer, and I want him to see me accomplish something while he’s still here. I want to become someone he can be proud of.

How can I take control of my life again and finally start moving forward?
comment: Spending 2.5 years preparing for one exam can quietly turn into a trap where your whole identity gets tied to one outcome. Maybe the goal now isn’t proving you’re disciplined overnight, but rebuilding trust with yourself through small promises you actually keep. A language school job could also be a step forward, not a defeat. Progress might come easier once life starts moving again.
